course_name_en: Measurement, Control and Regulation Technology I (MSR1)

learning_outcomes.text: Students possess basic knowledge for automation projects on products and processes.
In measurement technology, knowledge in the area of system description of sensors and transmission elements of the measurement chain.
In control technology, they have the physical-technical fundamentals for the description and design of control systems - and of dynamic systems in general.
Organize themselves in teams to perform practical experiments.
Apply personal competencies for communication, problem-solving, and decision-making.

syllabus_topics: Principle of regulation, principle of control, block diagram, standard control loop
Analog computers and operational amplifier circuits
Comparators, setpoint adjusters, transmission elements in general
Value range and operating point, linearization
Classification of system properties of transmission elements
Linear and nonlinear transmission elements, time-variant and time-invariant transmission elements
Investigation of transmission behavior through simulation
Differential equation as a parametric mathematical model
Application of Laplace transformation in control engineering
Inverse transformation into the time domain
Compilation of the most important transmission elements
P-element, P-T1-element, P-T2-element, I-elements, D-elements, dead-time elements
PID controllers and special cases of the PID controller
Understanding and implementing simple experimental setups; logging and evaluating measurements
Exercising appropriate communication skills, compiling and presenting work results.
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the written examination (grade). Active participation in the practical work is a prerequisite for taking the examination.
